---
title: Bank payouts
description: Add your bank once. The fee for that payout appears before you confirm.
---

You add your bank account once. When you pay out, the fee for that amount appears before you confirm.

## Add the account

Open Pay out. If there is no bank account yet, the screen asks you to add one and opens the bank form. You can also add it from Settings, then Payouts.

Enter the country of the bank, the name on the account, and the account number. A West African account is 24 characters and also needs the bank's SWIFT code. The account should be in the business name. You need a payout PIN first. Adding the account asks for that PIN.

The account is saved turned off. You cannot pay out to it until it is confirmed. A eurozone, UK, or Vietnam account is checked with the bank: a number that does not exist, or a name that is not the business, is refused. West African banks do not publish an account check, so a different name is still saved. The team gets an email to accept or refuse it. A number the bank says does not exist is refused.

Withdraw from the balance that matches the bank. A bank in Benin, Burkina Faso, Côte d'Ivoire, Guinea-Bissau, Mali, Niger, Senegal, or Togo pays F CFA. A eurozone bank pays euros. A US bank pays dollars. Convert first if the ledgers differ.

## What you pay

You receive the amount you enter. The fee is extra, and it comes out of the same balance.

The fee is the cost of sending that payout, then the higher of 25% above that cost or 0.5% of the amount. It is calculated when you type the amount. It is not a fixed price on your plan.

A local payout to one of those West African banks is in F CFA. The network does not add a payment fee on that local transfer. The cost is the exchange from euros into F CFA, about 1%. On 100,000 F CFA the fee is about 1,250 F CFA. You still receive 100,000 F CFA. The balance goes down by about 101,250 F CFA.

It usually arrives in 2 to 3 business days. It is not instant. Senegal, Burkina Faso, and Guinea-Bissau can take longer while the payment is checked.

A euro account in the eurozone can be sent as Instant. That fee is 1% of the amount, with a minimum of 1 EUR, and it usually arrives in minutes, including weekends and holidays. Standard on that same account takes a few business days.

Wave in Côte d'Ivoire is a separate payout, not this bank fee. A saved Wave number is 1%. A number you just added stays on a higher rate for 48 hours, then drops to 1%.

The same numbers are on the payout screen: you receive, the fee, and the total taken from the balance. Confirm only after that fee is on screen.
